what: Testing monotonicity of an instrumental variable
title: Data analysis and power analysis using RIQITE
text: use birth_school_age, data constructed match summary statistics reported Black et al. (2011) – Table 1 cross-tabulates month birth school entry age (early/-time/late), Table 3 reports total number subjects born January December (“discontinuity subsample”): 104,023, rounded 104,000, split evenly two birth months following Fiorini Stevens (2014). See ?birth_school_age details; reconstruction published aggregate proportions, set real individual records. following figure shows empirical distribution functions school-entry age December-born January-born subjects. figure, children started school older age born January rather December.  first perform standard regression analysis assessing relation instrument (birthday) school-entry age. conventionally considered persuasive evidence valid instrument. perform randomization test bounded null H≤0H_{\le 0} monotonicity instrument: difference--means statistic, Wilcoxon rank sum statistic, Stephenson rank sum statistic parameter s=10s = 10, along classical Student’s tt-test, producing Table 1 paper. Finally, infer effect range. range effect birth month school-entry age least year, indicating significant individual effect heterogeneity.
code: data(birth_school_age) dat <- birth_school_age table(dat$BirthMonth, dat$EntryTiming) #>       #>       Early  Late On-Time #>   Dec     0  7800   44200 #>   Jan  5200     0   46800 ggplot(dat, aes(EntryAge, color = BirthMonth, linetype = BirthMonth)) +   stat_ecdf(geom = "step", show.legend = FALSE, linewidth = 1.3) +   annotate("text", x = c(7.2, 7.2), y = c(.145, .81),            label = c("January", "December")) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(6, 8, .2)) +   theme_bw() +   theme(plot.background = element_blank(),         panel.grid.major = element_blank(),         panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),         plot.title = element_text(hjust = .5)) +   labs(x = "School-Entry Age (Years)", y = "Probability") lm.fit <- lm(EntryAge ~ (BirthMonth == "Dec"), dat) cat(paste(   "estimated average effect is", round(as.numeric(lm.fit$coefficients[2]), digits = 3),   "and F statistic is", round(as.numeric(summary(lm.fit)$fstatistic[1]), digits = 0),   "\n" )) #> estimated average effect is -0.667 and F statistic is 106256 dat$Z = as.numeric(dat$BirthMonth == "Dec") dat$Y = dat$EntryAge n <- length(dat$Z) m <- sum(dat$Z) # NOTE: the main paper uses nperm = 10^4; reduced here so the permutation # matrix (n x nperm) stays small enough to build quickly and with modest # memory in a vignette. nperm <- 10^3  Z.perm <- assign_CRE(n, m, nperm)  # difference-in-means pval.dim <- pval_bound(Z = dat$Z, Y = dat$Y, c = 0, method.list = list(name = "DIM"),                         alternative = "greater", Z.perm = Z.perm, impute = "control") ci.dim <- ci_bound(Z = dat$Z, Y = dat$Y, alternative = "greater", method.list = list(name = "DIM"),                     Z.perm = Z.perm, impute = "control", alpha = 0.10)  # Wilcoxon rank sum (Stephenson with s = 2) pval.wilc <- pval_quantile(Z = dat$Z, Y = dat$Y, k = n, c = 0, alternative = "greater",                             method.list = list(name = "Stephenson", s = 2), Z.perm = Z.perm) ci.wilc <- ci_quantile(Z = dat$Z, Y = dat$Y, k.vec = n, alternative = "greater",                         method.list = list(name = "Stephenson", s = 2), Z.perm = Z.perm, alpha = 0.10)  # Stephenson rank sum, s = 10 pval.steph10 <- pval_quantile(Z = dat$Z, Y = dat$Y, k = n, c = 0, alternative = "greater",                                method.list = list(name = "Stephenson", s = 10), Z.perm = Z.perm) ci.steph10 <- ci_quantile(Z = dat$Z, Y = dat$Y, k.vec = n, alternative = "greater",                            method.list = list(name = "Stephenson", s = 10), Z.perm = Z.perm, alpha = 0.10)  # classical Student's t-test ttest = t.test(dat$Y[dat$Z == 1], dat$Y[dat$Z == 0], alternative = "greater") pval.ttest = ttest$p.value ci.ttest = round(ttest$conf.int[1], digits = 3)  result = data.frame(test = c("diff-in-means", "Wilcoxon", "Stephenson 10", "t test"),                      pval = c(pval.dim, pval.wilc, pval.steph10, pval.ttest),                      lower = c(ci.dim, ci.wilc$lower, ci.steph10$lower, ci.ttest)) knitr::kable(result) tau.max.lower = ci_quantile(Z = dat$Z, Y = dat$Y, k.vec = n, alternative = "greater",                              method.list = list(name = "Stephenson", s = 10), Z.perm = Z.perm, alpha = 0.05)$lower tau.min.upper = ci_quantile(Z = dat$Z, Y = dat$Y, k.vec = 1, alternative = "less",                              method.list = list(name = "Stephenson", s = 10), Z.perm = Z.perm, alpha = 0.05)$upper print(paste("lower confidence limit for effect range is",             max(0, tau.max.lower - tau.min.upper))) #> [1] "lower confidence limit for effect range is 1.001"

text: next evaluate teacher professional development RCT treated teachers given professional development course electric circuits, Heller et al. (2012). cleaned data ships package.  standardize gain control-side variation outcome baseline, compare treatment control variation effect size units: correlation Yi(0)Y_i(0) τi\tau_i, standard deviation treatment impacts , using var(Yi(1))=var(Yi(0))+var(τi)var(Y_i(1)) = var(Y_i(0)) + var(\tau_i), around 0.28σ0.28\sigma effect size units (group standard deviations approximately 0.852 0.806):
code: data(electric_teachers)  mod <- lm(gain ~ TxAny, data = electric_teachers) est_ATE <- round(mod$coefficients[2], digits = 2) est_ATE #> TxAny  #> 19.77 hist(electric_teachers$gain[electric_teachers$TxAny == 1],      xlim = range(electric_teachers$gain), freq = FALSE, ylim = c(0, 0.065),      col = "grey", border = FALSE, breaks = 20,      main = NULL, xlab = "gain score") hist(electric_teachers$gain[electric_teachers$TxAny == 0],      freq = FALSE, add = TRUE, breaks = 20, col = NULL) sd_0 = sd(electric_teachers$Per.1[electric_teachers$TxAny == 0]) electric_teachers$std_gain = electric_teachers$gain / sd_0 electric_teachers %>% group_by(TxAny) %>%   summarise(raw_mean = mean(gain),             mean = mean(std_gain),             var = var(std_gain),             max = max(std_gain),             min = min(std_gain),             raw_sd = sd(gain),             sd = sd(std_gain)) #> # A tibble: 2 × 8 #>   TxAny raw_mean  mean   var   max    min raw_sd    sd #>   <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> #> 1     0     2.46 0.189 0.650  2.55 -1.79    10.5 0.806 #> 2     1    22.2  1.70  0.726  4.08 -0.510   11.1 0.852 tx_het <- sqrt(0.852^2 - 0.806^2) tx_het #> [1] 0.2761666

title: Data analysis and power analysis using RIQITE
text: plan using Stephenson’s Rank Sum test, need determine appropriate value ss. first conduct sensitivity analysis across range scenarios determine ss highest amount power top 10 quantiles, next 20 quantiles, next 40 quantiles. illustrate process, first run check best ss single scenario, using empirical distribution control outcomes normally-distributed, uncorrelated treatment effect (standardized units). get one row per targeted quantile explored ss, telling us easy detect effects quantile. performance 170th largest effect (233 effects): next make grid different scenarios explore see trends best ss consistent across different possible scenarios. grid scenarios used paper; simulation results shipped alongside vignette (heller_s_check_results.rds) vignette need re-run full multi-scenario simulation (considerably expensive single-scenario check ) every time built. aggregate findings see ss provides tightest confidence intervals across range quantile groups: top 10, next 20, next 30, next 40. group, take median median lower confidence bound. High points curve indicate ss informative:  can also tally winning ss across 100 quantiles exploring: Looking across results, wide range ss argued ; small ss costs us lower quantiles, large ss costs us across simulations. adjust ss try optimize multiple goals , using, e.g., s=6s = 6.

99):233) filter(res, k == 170) #> # A tibble: 9 × 6 #> # Groups:   s [9] #>       s     k power SEpower      q_ci     n #>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> #> 1     2   170  0     0      -Inf       40.4 #> 2     3   170  0     0        -1.23    51.0 #> 3     4   170  0.02  0.0133   -0.357   56.9 #> 4     5   170  0.19  0.0605   -0.158   59.6 #> 5     6   170  0.48  0.0904   -0.0350  62.2 #> 6     8   170  0.46  0.101    -0.0219  62.7 #> 7    10   170  0.43  0.0989   -0.0961  60.7 #> 8    15   170  0.17  0.0517   -0.246   53.2 #> 9    20   170  0.07  0.0396   -0.418   43.0 checks = expand_grid(TxVar = c(0.25, 0.75),                       tx_dist = c("rexp", "rnorm"),                       rho = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5)) # There is no treatment variation, nor correlation with Y0, when # the tx impact is a constant. checks = bind_rows(checks,                     tibble(TxVar = 0, tx_dist = "constant", rho = 0)) n_units = nrow(electric_teachers) s_selector = mutate(s_selector,                      group = cut(k,                                  breaks = c(0, 233 - 60, 233 - 30, 233 - 10, 233),                                  labels = c("v low", "low", "med", "high")))  s_selector$rho.f = factor(s_selector$rho,                            levels = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5),                            labels = c("rho = -0.5", "rho = 0", "rho = 0.5"))  avg = s_selector %>%   group_by(s, group, rho, rho.f) %>%   summarise(q_ci = median(q_ci), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%   filter(group != "v low")  s_agg = s_selector %>%   group_by(s, group, rho, rho.f, tx_dist) %>%   summarise(q_ci = median(q_ci), .groups = "drop")  s_agg %>%   filter(group != "v low") %>%   ggplot(aes(s, q_ci)) +   facet_grid(rho.f ~ group) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +   geom_line(aes(col = tx_dist), linewidth = 0.5) +   labs(x = "s", y = "Median lower CI bound", col = "Tx distribution:") +   scale_x_log10(breaks = unique(s_selector$s)) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +   geom_point(data = avg, col = "black", size = 2) +   coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1.5, 2)) +   theme(legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm"),         panel.border = element_rect(colour = "grey", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)) qis <- s_selector %>%   group_by(TxVar, tx_dist, rho, group, k) %>%   filter(q_ci == max(q_ci)) table(group = qis$group, s = qis$s, rho = qis$rho) #> , , rho = -0.5 #>  #>        s #> group    2  3  4  5  6  8 10 15 20 #>   v low  0  0  0  0  1 39 57 31 32 #>   low    0  0  6 36 66 12  0  0  0 #>   med    1 30 39 10  0  0  0  0  0 #>   high  27 13  0  0  0  0  0  0  0 #>  #> , , rho = 0 #>  #>        s #> group    2  3  4  5  6  8 10 15 20 #>   v low  0  0  0  0  0 43 63 51 43 #>   low    0  0  0 15 66 68  1  0  0 #>   med    0  0 11 48 17 24  0  0  0 #>   high   0  6  5 17  1 13  3  5  0 #>  #> , , rho = 0.5 #>  #>        s #> group    2  3  4  5  6  8 10 15 20 #>   v low  0  0  0  0  0 25 48 48 39 #>   low    0  0  0  0 32 87  1  0  0 #>   med    0  0  0  7 33 40  0  0  0 #>   high   0  0  1  1 12 14  8  3  1
